question: A combination of vehicles falls into CDL Class A when the gross combination weight rating (GCWR) is 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the towed vehicle(s) exceeds what weight?
choice_d: 5,000 pounds
explanation: Class A applies to combination vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than 10,000 pounds.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle weighing 10,000 pounds GVWR or less, falls into which CDL class?
choice_d: It does not require a CDL
explanation: Class B (Heavy Straight Vehicles) covers any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR less than 26,001 pounds is included in the CDL program as a Class C vehicle only if it meets which condition?
choice_a: It is used exclusively for interstate commerce
choice_b: It is designed to carry 16 or more passengers (including the driver), or it transports hazardous materials requiring placarding
choice_c: It has more than two axles
choice_d: It is owned by a for-hire motor carrier
explanation: Class C vehicles under 26,001 pounds GVWR are included in the CDL program only if designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding (or select agents/toxins).
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: What is the minimum CDL disqualification period for a first violation of a railroad-highway grade crossing law?
choice_d: 1 year
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least 60 days for a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: A driver who wants to haul material designated as hazardous and required to be placarded must add which endorsement, after passing a special written examination on recognizing, handling, and transporting such material?
choice_d: Doubles/Triples (T)
explanation: Any driver hauling material designated hazardous and required to be placarded under 49 CFR part 172 must add a Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement and pass a special written exam on recognizing, handling, and transporting such material.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Which endorsement must a Class A driver add in order to pull double or triple trailers, after passing a special knowledge exam on the problems of pulling multiple trailers?
choice_d: Passenger (P)
explanation: Drivers qualified for Class A who wish to pull double or triple trailers must add the Doubles and Triples (T) endorsement after passing a special knowledge exam on the problems of pulling multiple trailers.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement is required for transporting liquid or gaseous material in a tank meeting which capacity thresholds?
choice_a: An individual tank rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more
choice_c: An individual tank rated capacity of more than 1,000 gallons only
choice_d: An aggregate rated capacity of more than 119 gallons only
explanation: The N endorsement applies to vehicles transporting liquid or gaseous material in a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A driver must add a Passenger (P) endorsement if they wish to drive a vehicle with a design capacity to carry how many people, including the driver?
choice_d: 20 or more
explanation: Drivers who wish to drive a vehicle with a design capacity to carry 16 or more people, including the driver, must add a Passenger (P) endorsement.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: The School Bus (S) endorsement applies to applicants who wish to drive a school bus in which CDL class(es)?
choice_d: Class C only
explanation: The School Bus (S) endorsement applies to applicants who wish to drive a school bus in any class (A, B, or C).
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Drivers of tank vehicles who haul hazardous materials or waste in amounts requiring placards must add which endorsement, showing they passed exams for both tank vehicles and hazardous materials?
choice_d: Doubles/Triples (T)
explanation: The X endorsement is required for drivers of tank vehicles who haul hazardous materials or waste requiring placards, showing they passed the special knowledge exams for both tank vehicles and hazardous materials.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Which three endorsements are the only ones that may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_b: Passenger (P), School bus (S), and Tank vehicle (N)
choice_d: All six endorsements may be added to a CLP
explanation: The manual specifies that the only endorsements that may be added to a CLP are Passenger (P), School bus (S), and Tank vehicle (N).
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: If a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) is issued with a Tanker (N) endorsement, what restriction must also be included on it?
choice_b: X - no cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
choice_c: L - no air brake equipped CMV
choice_d: P - no passengers in a CMV bus
explanation: A CLP issued with a Tanker (N) endorsement must also contain the X restriction, meaning the holder may only operate an empty, purged tank vehicle.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: If a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) is issued with a Passenger (P) or School Bus (S) endorsement, it must also contain which restriction?
choice_a: P - no passengers in a CMV bus
choice_b: X - no cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
choice_d: Z - no full air brake equipped CMV
explanation: A CLP issued with a Passenger (P) or School Bus (S) endorsement must also contain the P restriction, prohibiting the CLP holder from carrying passengers other than specified exceptions like auditors, examiners, or trainees.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: If an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission, what restriction must the State indicate on the CDL if issued?
choice_b: L - no air brake equipped CMV
choice_d: M - no Class A passenger vehicle
explanation: If the skills test is performed in a vehicle with an automatic transmission, the E restriction is added, prohibiting the driver from operating a CMV equipped with a manual transmission.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: What restriction is placed on a CDL/CLP if the applicant does not take or fails the air brake portion of the knowledge test, or performs the skills test in a vehicle without air brakes?
choice_a: L - no air brake equipped CMV
choice_b: Z - no full air brake equipped CMV
choice_d: O - no tractor trailer CMV
explanation: The L restriction is applied when an applicant does not take or fails the air brake test, or tests in a vehicle not equipped with air brakes, restricting them from operating any CMV equipped with air brakes.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: If an applicant performs the Group A skills test in a combination vehicle connected by a pintle hook rather than a fifth wheel, what restriction is added to the CDL?
choice_a: N - no Class A and B passenger vehicle
choice_c: M - no Class A passenger vehicle
choice_d: K - intrastate only
explanation: If the power unit and towed unit are connected with a pintle hook or other non-fifth-wheel connection during the Group A skills test, the O restriction is added, prohibiting operation of a fifth-wheel tractor-trailer combination.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: What restriction applies if an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with air-over-hydraulic brakes?
choice_a: L - no air brake equipped CMV
choice_b: Z - no full air brake equipped CMV
choice_d: V - medical variance
explanation: The Z restriction applies when the skills test is performed in a vehicle with air-over-hydraulic brakes, restricting the driver from operating a CMV with any braking system operating fully on the air brake principle.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: Which of the following will cause a driver to be denied or lose a hazardous materials endorsement under the TSA background check requirements?
choice_a: Having fewer than two years of driving experience
choice_b: Not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States
choice_d: Failing the air brakes knowledge test
explanation: The manual lists not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States as one of the grounds for being denied or losing a hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-9

question: The CDL Skills Test consists of three segments that must be taken and passed in order before moving to the next. What is that order?
choice_a: On-road driving, basic vehicle control, vehicle inspection
choice_b: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, on-road driving
choice_c: Basic vehicle control, on-road driving, vehicle inspection
choice_d: Vehicle inspection, on-road driving, basic vehicle control
explanation: The manual states the Skills Test segments must be taken in the order listed: vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving, with each passed before moving to the next.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: Drivers who operate in non-excepted interstate commerce are required to provide which document to their State Driver Licensing Agency (SDLA)?
choice_a: A current medical examiner's certificate (49 CFR 391.45), commonly called a DOT card
choice_d: An International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA) license
explanation: Drivers who operate in non-excepted interstate commerce are required to provide a current medical examiner's certificate (49 CFR 391.45), commonly referred to as a medical certificate or DOT card, to their SDLA.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: A driver who self-certifies as "Intrastate excepted" is making which certification?
choice_a: That they operate entirely in intrastate commerce, are not subject to the medical requirements for their State, and are not required to obtain a medical examiner's certificate
choice_b: That they operate in interstate commerce and are required to obtain a medical certificate
choice_c: That they operate entirely in intrastate commerce and are required to obtain a medical examiner's certificate
choice_d: That they operate in both interstate and intrastate commerce
explanation: The Intrastate excepted self-certification statement certifies that the driver operates entirely in intrastate commerce, is not subject to the State's medical requirements, and is not required to obtain a medical examiner's certificate.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes it illegal to operate a CMV, and what is the minimum CDL loss for a first offense at or above this level?
choice_d: .02% BAC; at least 6 months
explanation: It is illegal to operate a CMV with a BAC of .04% or more, and a driver will lose their CDL for at least one year for a first offense of driving at or above this level.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: If a disqualifying offense such as driving under the influence occurs while the driver is operating a CMV that is placarded for hazardous materials, what is the minimum CDL disqualification period?
choice_d: 5 years
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least three years if the disqualifying offense occurs while operating a CMV that is placarded for hazardous materials.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: What is the CDL disqualification consequence of committing a second offense among the listed alcohol/felony violations (such as DUI, refusing alcohol testing, or leaving the scene of an accident)?
choice_c: Loss of the CDL for life
choice_d: A $5,000 fine only, with no license loss
explanation: The manual states that a driver will lose their CDL for life for a second offense of the listed alcohol, leaving the scene, or felony violations.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: What happens to a driver who has any detectable amount of alcohol below .04% BAC while operating a CMV?
choice_a: They are put out-of-service for 24 hours
choice_b: They receive an immediate lifetime disqualification
choice_c: They receive a written warning only
choice_d: They lose their CDL for 90 days
explanation: The manual states a driver will be put out-of-service for 24 hours if they have any detectable amount of alcohol under .04%.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: What is the minimum CDL disqualification for committing two serious traffic violations (such as excessive speeding of 15 mph or more over the posted limit) within a three-year period involving a CMV?
choice_d: 1 year
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least 60 days if they have committed two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: What is the minimum CDL disqualification for a first violation of an out-of-service order?
choice_d: 1 year
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least 90 days for a first violation of an out-of-service order.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: What is the consequence for a CDL holder who is found to have more than one driver's license?
choice_a: A court may fine the driver up to $5,000 or put them in jail, and the state will keep the home state license and return any others
choice_b: Automatic lifetime CDL disqualification with no fine
choice_d: No penalty as long as the licenses are from different states
explanation: The manual states that CDL holders cannot have more than one license; violating this rule can result in a court fine of up to $5,000 or jail, with the home state license kept and any others returned.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-10
